"FORMULA 1: THROUGH THE GENERATIONS

Ultimate Formula Racing Evolution Game

Create a fully playable, immersive 3D Formula 1 racing game that takes players through the entire history of Formula 1, from the legendary early generations of the 1950s to the modern era of 2026.

The game must combine realistic racing, career progression, historical accuracy, car development, team management, track evolution and exciting Grand Prix weekends.

1. THE GENERATIONS OF FORMULA 1

Divide the game into historical eras. Each era must have its own authentic cars, racing physics, engine sounds, visual style, circuits and regulations.

Era 1: The Golden Pioneers (1950–1960)

- Front-engine racing machines.
- Minimal safety equipment.
- Narrow tyres and exposed cockpits.
- Classic racing circuits.
- Raw mechanical engine sounds.

Era 2: The Revolution (1961–1970)

- Rear-engine cars.
- Introduction of aerodynamic wings.
- Increasing engine performance.
- Classic racing liveries.

Era 3: The Turbo and Groundbreaking Era (1971–1980)

- Powerful V8 and V12 engines.
- Introduction of turbo technology.
- Experimental aerodynamic designs.
- Increasingly competitive racing.

Era 4: The Turbo Monsters (1981–1990)

- Extremely powerful turbocharged engines.
- Aggressive aerodynamic designs.
- Legendary rivalries.
- Dramatic turbo boost and engine sounds.

Era 5: The Modernisation Era (1991–2000)

- Advanced aerodynamics.
- Improved safety.
- Semi-automatic gearboxes.
- More sophisticated suspension and handling.

Era 6: The V10 Era (2001–2008)

- Screaming naturally aspirated V10 engines.
- High-revving racing machines.
- Slick tyres.
- Advanced aerodynamic packages.

Era 7: The Hybrid Revolution (2009–2016)

- Introduction of KERS.
- Transition to V6 turbo-hybrid engines.
- Energy recovery systems.
- Changing aerodynamic regulations.

Era 8: The Aero Revolution (2017–2021)

- Wider cars and tyres.
- Massive aerodynamic performance.
- Powerful hybrid engines.
- High-speed cornering.

Era 9: The Ground Effect Era (2022–2026)

- Modern ground-effect aerodynamics.
- Advanced hybrid power units.
- DRS and energy deployment systems.
- Modern safety technology and sophisticated race strategies.

2. CAREER MODE

Start as a completely unknown racing driver.

Build your reputation from the bottom:

- Start with historic junior racing categories.
- Earn opportunities to join Formula 1 teams.
- Sign contracts with different teams.
- Improve your driving reputation.
- Compete for championships.
- Become a legendary world champion.

Allow players to choose their starting generation or begin in 1950 and unlock each era chronologically.

Your career should evolve with the sport.

3. CAR DEVELOPMENT

Give players the ability to develop and upgrade their cars.

Development categories:

- Engine performance.
- Turbo systems.
- Aerodynamics.
- Front and rear wings.
- Suspension.
- Brakes.
- Tyre performance.
- Gearbox.
- Reliability.
- Fuel efficiency.

Each historical era must have different development possibilities. Do not allow modern technology in older generations.

Car performance must reflect the technology available during that particular era.

4. GRAND PRIX WEEKENDS

Every race weekend should feature:

Practice 1, 2 and 3

- Test different setups.
- Experiment with tyres.
- Learn the circuit.
- Collect performance data.

Qualifying

- Q1, Q2 and Q3 where historically appropriate.
- Earlier generations should use their own qualifying formats.
- Fight for pole position.

Race Day

- Formation lap.
- Starting grid.
- Five red lights.
- Race start.
- Pit stops.
- Tyre strategies.
- Safety cars.
- Weather changes.
- Mechanical failures.
- Chequered flag.
- Podium celebrations.

5. HISTORICALLY ACCURATE CIRCUITS

Include circuits that evolved throughout Formula 1 history.

Examples:

- Monaco.
- Monza.
- Silverstone.
- Spa-Francorchamps.
- Nürburgring.
- Suzuka.
- Interlagos.
- Imola.
- Zandvoort.
- Melbourne.
- Circuit of the Americas.

Some circuits must have different layouts depending on the selected year.

6. RACING EXPERIENCE

Create realistic 3D racing with:

- Cockpit camera.
- Driver helmet camera.
- TV broadcast camera.
- Chase camera.
- Trackside cameras.

Include realistic:

- Tyre degradation.
- Fuel consumption.
- Engine temperatures.
- Mechanical wear.
- Brake temperatures.
- Wet and dry weather.
- Damage modelling.
- Grip changes.
- Overtaking and defensive driving.

Cars from different generations must feel completely different to drive.

7. HISTORICAL RIVALRIES

Introduce legendary historical drivers, teams and rivalries.

Build a historical championship database with famous drivers, iconic cars, championship standings and memorable racing moments.

Allow players to recreate famous championship battles or rewrite F1 history with their own career.

Use fictional team and driver alternatives if official licensing is unavailable.

8. GAME MODES

- Career Mode.
- Historical Championship Mode.
- Single Grand Prix.
- Custom Championship.
- Time Trial.
- Classic Car Challenges.
- Multiplayer Racing.
- Create Your Own Championship.

9. VISUALS AND SOUND

Create beautiful, realistic 3D environments.

Every generation must visually reflect its time period:

- Old-fashioned grandstands and circuits.
- Historic pit garages.
- Period-correct advertising boards.
- Era-specific racing suits and helmets.
- Authentic car designs and sounds.

Modern generations should feature advanced lighting, realistic reflections, detailed cockpits and high-quality track environments.

10. PROGRESSION AND UNLOCKS

Reward players for:

- Winning races.
- Setting fastest laps.
- Winning championships.
- Breaking lap records.
- Completing historic challenges.

Unlock legendary cars, alternative liveries, helmets, circuits and special racing events.

IMPORTANT GAME DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS

- Fully playable 3D racing game.
- Mobile-friendly controls and interface.
- Responsive steering, braking and acceleration.
- Realistic AI opponents that defend, attack and make mistakes.
- Complete championship progression.
- Save career progress.
- Functional pit stops and tyre strategies.
- Different physics and handling for every generation.
- Optimised performance for mobile devices.

The most important feature: This must not feel like one modern F1 game with different-looking cars. Every generation must feel like a completely different chapter in the evolution of Formula 1 racing.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh` — invokes the runtime capture script; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`, `CAPTURE_URL`, and `CAPTURE_DIR`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.omgithub/scripts/default-start.mjs` — defines the supported app types, Vite build behavior, and serves the app on port 3000 by default.

## Run and test

For the configured runtime, run `./start.sh` with `RUNTIME_DIR` set; the default server uses port **3000**. Its runtime script builds Vite projects before serving them. `capture.sh` can capture the running app when supplied the capture URL and output directory. `Agents.md` also documents Playwright CLI screenshot checks; it mentions port 3002 for a Pascal development server, so use the actual port for this app.

## Recommendation

Start with a root `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` for a lightweight browser game, or add a Vite scaffold if the game benefits from modular code. A Canvas 2D implementation is a practical fit for an arcade-style F1 game: draw the circuit and cars procedurally, then add keyboard controls, laps/timing, and collision boundaries. ## Objective
- Complete a playable Formula 1 history racing game spanning 1950–2026, with era-specific gameplay, career progression, race modes, and mobile-friendly controls.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing browser game; use reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Validate interactions, responsive layout, and JavaScript console; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use a lightweight static browser app with procedural Canvas graphics and no external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names provide contextual tribute.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented home, era/weekend selectors, career, garage, history, race HUD/modals, and responsive styling.
- Added career persistence (`f1-generations-career`), race setup, input bindings, countdown, race physics, AI movement, Canvas circuit/car rendering, telemetry, pit stops, results, scoring, and synthesized engine audio.

- Fix and validate race countdown and gameplay behavior; the countdown rendering expects `.on` lamp classes, but CSS has no `.on` rule and lamps are toggled without that class.
- Test app interactions and mobile/desktop layout in a browser; inspect console output.
- Capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot ≤1280px wide, fixing any issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser validation and screenshot are pending.

- Complete a playable Formula 1 history racing game spanning 1950–2026, with era-specific gameplay, career progression, race modes, and mobile-friendly controls.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing browser game using reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Validate interactions, responsive layout, and JavaScript console; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

- Use a lightweight static browser app with procedural Canvas graphics and no external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names provide contextual tribute.

### Completed
- Implemented home, era/weekend selectors, career, garage, history, race HUD/modals, and responsive styling.

- (none)

- Complete a playable Formula 1 history racing game spanning 1950–2026, with era-specific gameplay, career progression, race modes, and mobile-friendly controls.
